chunks: One of our companions narrated from Ḥanān, who said: My father Miskān narrated to him from a man

that they were in the house of Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) and Muyassir was among them. They spoke about keeping ties with near kinsfolk, so Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muyassir, your death had arrived on more than one occasion, but each time it was postponed for you by Allah due to your keeping ties with your near relatives.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh (Imam al-Ṣādiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of maintaining ties with relatives according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reveals to Muyassir that his prolonged life was a divine reprieve specifically granted as a reward for maintaining family ties (*silat al-qaribah*). This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on kinship not merely as a social duty, but as a spiritual mechanism that can alter one's destiny and delay death, linking personal piety directly to familial bonds.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 26.One of our companions narrated from Ḥanān who said, “Ibn Muskān narrated to us from another man, that they were in the house of Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) and Muyassir was among them. They spoke about the subject of keeping ties with near kinsfolk, so Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) said, ‘O Muyassir, your death had arrived on more than one occasion, but each time it was postponed for you by Allah due to your keeping ties with your near relatives.’”
